sources_considered.why: Read the published abstract; cite the dated arXiv record of the same research below.
Controlled comparison of English and altered languages at multiple training stages.
Independent crosslinguistic follow-up corroborates a limited human-like learning preference.
Identifies a confound in a prominent comparison in the first study.
Tests coherence of learned world models and documents failures under related tasks.
Reports positive world-model results in restricted text environments; relevant to the limits of the world-understanding assertion.

Read as a further methodological check. Its grammaticality and generation tests do not establish broad world understanding; the earlier independent language-learning studies suffice for the proposed narrow contradiction.

evidence_items.explanation: Kallini and colleagues compared GPT-2 learning across English and systematically altered languages, including different training stages. The observed preference conflicts with the language-learning component under the stated family-level interpretation.

Yang and colleagues extended testing to 12 languages from four families and found partial discrimination between attested and impossible patterns. This independently corroborates a preference, while explicitly rejecting equivalence with human learning.

Hunter identifies a confound between counting rules and non-adjacent dependencies. This limits claims that the initial experiment demonstrates specifically human grammatical constraints, although that stronger conclusion is not required by the ordinary preference criterion.

Vafa and colleagues find weaknesses in world-model coherence across game, logic and navigation settings. These findings support concern about tested systems but cannot establish failure at every future training scale.

Li and colleagues report coherent state tracking and useful simulation in five text environments after targeted training. The restricted environments and dependence on training coverage prevent treating this as decisive evidence of broad world understanding.

unresolved_gaps: The cited results do not settle whether GPT-style systems can develop broad cohesive world understanding.
The language studies establish limited preferences, not the full set of constraints governing human language acquisition.
The outcome would change if systems like GPT-3 were restricted to the original GPT-3 checkpoint or gravitate required an exclusively human learning capacity.
